question: In which of the following years did Sri Aurobindo resign from his post in Baroda and move to Calcutta and there he soon became a prominent leader of the nationalist movement? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (18/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: 1906
1916
1914
1910
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1906

Explanation:
Sri Aurobindo Ghosh resigned from his post in Baroda in 1906 and moved to Calcutta, where he soon became a prominent leader of the nationalist movement. He opposed the partition of Bengal, became editor of the newspaper 'Vande Mataram', and advocated for Swadeshi, boycott, and national education. His ideas gave a new direction to the Indian freedom struggle. Later, he turned to spirituality and settled in Pondicherry.

question: Which region witnessed the strongest violence and martial law enforcement during the Rowlatt Satyagraha?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (18/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Bihar
Bengal
Punjab
Gujarat
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Punjab

Explanation:
During the Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919), the strongest violence and martial law enforcement occurred in Punjab. Gandhiji called for a nationwide strike on 6 April 1919 to protest the Rowlatt Act. In Amritsar, on 10 April, firing on protesters led to widespread violence and casualties. The British government imposed martial law in Punjab, which included press censorship, ban on public meetings, and brutal repression. The most infamous event was the Jallianwala Bagh massacre on 13 April 1919, where General Dyer ordered his troops to fire on unarmed civilians, killing hundreds. Punjab experienced the longest period of martial law and the harshest suppression during the Rowlatt Satyagraha.

☛ Who attempted to assassinate General Dyer? → Udham Singh
question_hi: रोलेट सत्याग्रह के दौरान किस क्षेत्र में सबसे प्रबल हिंसा और मार्शल लॉ लागू किया गया था? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (18/08/2025) Shift 3)

Explanation:

question: Which harmful social practice was banned in 1829 by Lord Bentinck during the British rule in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (18/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Child marriage
Polygamy
Dowry
Sati
solution:

Explanation:
In 1829, Lord William Bentinck banned the Sati practice, where a widow was forced to immolate herself on her husband's funeral pyre. This cruel social custom was abolished due to efforts of social reformers like Raja Ram Mohan Roy. Bentinck declared it illegal in the Bengal Presidency and later extended to all of India. This step was a landmark in social reforms during British rule.

question: Which event is considered the turning point in Gandhi’s political life, converting him from a moderate to a mass leader?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Jallianwala Bagh Massacre
Salt Satyagraha
Rowlatt Act protest
Champaran Satyagraha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Champaran Satyagraha

Explanation:
Champaran Satyagraha (1917) was Gandhi’s first successful satyagraha in India. It was against the exploitation of peasants in the Champaran district of Bihar who were forced to grow indigo under the tinkathia system. Gandhi led a nonviolent protest against the British, resulting in the abolition of the oppressive system. This event marked the turning point in Gandhi's political life, transforming him from a moderate to a mass leader. After this, he led the Kheda Satyagraha (1918) and the Rowlatt Act protest (1919). Champaran Satyagraha gave Gandhi national recognition and paved the way for mass participation in the Indian freedom movement.

question: Which body was formed by Gandhi on 24 February 1919 to oppose the Rowlatt Act?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Congress Committee
Swaraj Sabha
Khilafat Committee
Satyagraha Sabha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Satyagraha Sabha

Explanation:
On 24 February 1919, Gandhi formed the Satyagraha Sabha to oppose the Rowlatt Act. This act was passed in 1919 and contained stringent provisions such as arrest without trial. Gandhi called for Satyagraha against it and organized the movement through the Satyagraha Sabha. A hartal was observed in Delhi on 30 March 1919 and across the country on 6 April. This movement laid the foundation for the Non-Cooperation Movement. Gandhi believed the Rowlatt Act violated civil liberties. The Satyagraha Sabha organized signature campaigns and public meetings for peaceful protest.

question: In which of the following years was the first British East India Company founded in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: 1620
1600
1605
1588
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1600

Explanation:
The British East India Company was founded on December 31, 1600, during the reign of Queen Elizabeth I of England. It was granted the name 'Governor and Company of Merchants of London Trading into the East Indies'. The company received a monopoly on trade with India, valid for 15 years. Sir James Lancaster was its first governor. The primary objective of the company was to trade in spices, silk, cotton cloth, and other goods. Later, this company became the foundation of the British Empire in India.

question: In organising the Rowlatt Satyagraha, Mahatma Gandhi was assisted by Abdul Bari of the Firangi Ulema group based in _________. (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Kanpur
Patna
Aligarh
Lucknow
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lucknow

Explanation:
In organising the Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919), Mahatma Gandhi was assisted by Abdul Bari of the Firangi Ulema group based in Lucknow. Abdul Bari was a prominent Muslim religious leader, and the Firangi Ulema group, centered in Lucknow, supported Gandhi's opposition to the Rowlatt Act. This collaboration strengthened Hindu-Muslim unity and gave the Satyagraha widespread public support. The Rowlatt Act was passed in 1919, allowing arrest and deportation without trial. Gandhi called for a strike and prayer on 6 April 1919 against this repressive law. The Satyagraha was one of the first nationwide movements led by Gandhi, paving the way for the Non-Cooperation Movement.

question: Dating back to 1639-1640 CE, which construction, located in Chennai, India, is historically known as the primary English defense post? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 2)

question: Which of the following freedom fighters led the Rampa Rebellion of 1922 against forest laws? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 2)

question: Who was the first Portuguese explorer to reach India in 1498, arriving at Calicut on the Malabar Coast? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Columbus
Vasco da Gama
Nino-da-Cunha
Albuquerque
solution:

Explanation:
Vasco da Gama was a Portuguese explorer who reached India in 1498 by sea route, arriving at Calicut (now Kozhikode) on the Malabar Coast. His voyage established the first direct sea route from Europe to Asia, giving Portugal control over the spice trade. This event marked a turning point in world history, as it initiated the era of European colonialism in India. Da Gama's expedition was sponsored by King Manuel I of Portugal. He later returned to India as viceroy in 1524. Calicut was a major trading port for spices like pepper and cardamom, which were highly valued in Europe.

question_hi: राममोहन राय ने 1803 में किस दार्शनिक कृति में तर्क और सामाजिक प्रासंगिकता के माध्यम से विश्व धर्मों का विश्लेषण किया? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (20/08/2025) Shift 2)

question: The Partition of Bengal (1905) was justified by the British on the basis of __________. (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (20/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Economic prosperity
Religious harmony
Administrative facility
Spread of education
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Administrative facility

Explanation:
The Partition of Bengal in 1905 was officially justified by the British on the grounds of administrative facility. Viceroy Lord Curzon argued that the Bengal Presidency was too large, making efficient administration difficult. However, the real motive was to foster Hindu-Muslim division and weaken the nationalist movement. The partition created a new province of Eastern Bengal and Assam, with a Muslim majority. This sparked widespread protests and the Swadeshi movement. The partition was eventually annulled in 1911.

question: Which trio of leaders is famously associated with the rise of Extremist ideology in Indian nationalism? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 1)

Gokhale-Tilak-Gandhi
Nehru-Gandhi-Patel
Aurobindo-Lajpat Rai-Gokhale
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lal-Bal-Pal

Explanation:
The trio famously associated with the rise of Extremist ideology in Indian nationalism is Lal-Bal-Pal. It comprised Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Bipin Chandra Pal. These three leaders became symbols of militant nationalism in the early 20th century. They advocated programs like Swaraj, boycott, Swadeshi, and national education. Tilak gave the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'. Lala Lajpat Rai was known as 'Punjab Kesari'. Bipin Chandra Pal was a prominent extremist leader from Bengal. They played a key role in the split of the Indian National Congress at the Surat session of 1907 and fiercely opposed British rule. Their efforts significantly shaped the Extremist phase of the Indian freedom struggle.

options_hi: सोशल सर्विस लीग

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है यंग बंगाल मूवमेंट

Explanation:
हेनरी विवियन डेरोजियो कोलकाता के हिंदू कॉलेज में शिक्षक थे। उन्होंने अपने छात्रों को कट्टरपंथी विचारों से प्रेरित किया और उन्हें सभी अधिकार पर सवाल उठाने के लिए प्रोत्साहित किया। इस आंदोलन को यंग बंगाल मूवमेंट कहा गया। यह 1820 के दशक में शुरू हुआ और इसके अनुयायियों को यंग बंगाल या डेरोजियन कहा गया। उन्होंने सामाजिक सुधार, महिला शिक्षा, जाति प्रथा के उन्मूलन और तर्कसंगत सोच पर जोर दिया। डेरोजियो ने अकादमिक एसोसिएशन की स्थापना की और छात्रों के बीच स्वतंत्र विचार को बढ़ावा दिया। यह आंदोलन बंगाल के पुनर्जागरण का एक महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा था।

question: The main objective of British economic policies in India was to: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: support rural employment
promote Indian self-sufficiency
benefit the British economy
industrialise India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is benefit the British economy

Explanation:
The main objective of British economic policies in India was to turn India into a source of raw materials and a market for finished goods for Britain. Under this policy, raw materials like cotton, indigo, and tea were exported from India at cheap prices, while finished textiles and industrial products from Britain were sold in India. This policy destroyed Indian industries, especially the handloom industry. British officials exploited India economically through land revenue systems and trade policies. This policy was contrary to Indian self-sufficiency and industrialisation. It ensured that India remained a supplier of raw materials and a consumer of British manufactured goods, thereby strengthening the British economy at the cost of India's economic development.

question_hi: भारत में ब्रिटिश आर्थिक नीतियों का मुख्य उद्देश्य था: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: ग्रामीण रोजगार का समर्थन करना।
भारतीय आत्मनिर्भरता को बढ़ावा देना।
ब्रिटिश अर्थव्यवस्था को लाभ पहुंचाना।
भारत का औद्योगीकरण करना।
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है ब्रिटिश अर्थव्यवस्था को लाभ पहुंचाना

Explanation:
ब्रिटिश आर्थिक नीतियों का मुख्य उद्देश्य भारत को ब्रिटेन का कच्चे माल का स्रोत और तैयार माल का बाजार बनाना था। इसके तहत भारत से कपास, नील, चाय आदि कच्चा माल सस्ते दामों पर निर्यात किया जाता था, जबकि ब्रिटेन से तैयार वस्त्र और औद्योगिक उत्पाद भारत में बेचे जाते थे। इस नीति ने भारतीय उद्योगों, विशेषकर हथकरघा उद्योग, को बर्बाद कर दिया। ब्रिटिश अधिकारियों ने लगान व्यवस्था और व्यापार नीतियों के माध्यम से भारत का आर्थिक शोषण किया। यह नीति भारत के आत्मनिर्भरता और औद्योगीकरण के विपरीत थी।
